full_story_part1.text: If you're going to learn English words, start with the ones people use a lot. That's obviously right. There's no arguing with it. And yet, the moment a gacha appears in front of you, the good student inside you steps away. That may be true, but what's the rarest one? Wait. You came here to study today, didn't you? The Dopa English Word Gacha is just the thing to send your mind off track. English word cards have 7 rarity levels. The more often a word is used, the lower its level. the less often it is used, the higher. The words you'd want to learn first for study end up on the dull side in the gacha. Practical value and star power, surprisingly, live apart. Normally, you might think, Could I use this in conversation? But now you might lean forward and think, What? This word is hardly ever used! You check the rarity before reading the meaning. You thought you were opening a vocabulary book, but in your mind, a send-off for the rare-word hunters is already underway.

full_story_part2.text: What's more, when you draw a card rated UR or higher, the bonus Jackpot begins, and you can keep opening packs. You're happy about one rare card, and then you get more time to open packs. Your willpower is just about to stand up and say, All right, time to review, when Just one more tugs at its sleeve. What might happen here is not that you lose interest in English words. It's that the reason for your interest changes. You go from I draw a card because I want to learn to I look at words because I want to draw a card. Even if you're looking at the same cards, the person in charge inside your mind has changed from the study worker to the treasure hunter. But here's something worth underlining in red. Just because a word is rare doesn't mean it should be high on your study list. Rarity is simply the game's way of sorting words by how often they are used. I'm happy I drew it and I should learn it first are 2 separate things. Even if it shines, it doesn't get special treatment in your study order.
